id: http://arxiv.org/abs/2007.04276v2
published: 2020-07-08T17:22:02Z
summary: The problem of objectivity, i.e. how to explain on quantum grounds the objective character of the macroscopic world, is one of the aspects of the celebrated quantum-to-classical transition. Initiated by W. H. Zurek and collaborators, this problem gained some attention recently with several approaches being developed. The aim of this work is to compare three of them: quantum Darwinism, Spectrum Broadcast Structures, and strong quantum Darwinism. The paper is concentrated on foundations, providing a synthetic analysis of how the three approaches realize the idea of objectivity and how they are related to each other. As a byproduct of this analysis, a proof of a generalized Spectrum Broadcast Structure theorem is presented. Recent quantum Darwinism experiments are also briefly discussed.

title: Objectivity (or lack there of): a comparison between predictions of quantum Darwinism and spectrum broadcast structure
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/1803.00765v2
published: 2018-03-02T09:08:47Z
summary: Quantum Darwinism and spectrum broadcast structure describe the emergence of objectivity in quantum systems. However, it is unclear whether these two frameworks lead to consistent predictions on the objectivity of the state of a quantum system in a given scenario. In this paper, we jointly investigate quantum Darwinism and spectrum broadcasting, as well as the subdivision of quantum Darwinism into accessible information and quantum discord, in a two-level system interacting with an $N$-level environment via a random matrix coupling. We propose a novel partial trace method to suitably and consistently partition the effective $N$-level environment, and compare the predictions with those obtained using the partitioning method proposed by Perez [Phys. Decomposition-Indexed Classicality: An A/R/F Framework for Observer-Dependent Quantum Experience
Authors/Creators
Almon, Ricardo
(Producer)
Contributors
Producer:
Almon, Ricardo
Description
This work develops a quantitative framework for
observer-dependent classicality
in quantum mechanics based on three operational functionals:
Redundancy (R)
,
Accessibility (A)
, and
Observer Flow (F)
. The A/R/F framework distinguishes environmental redundancy from the effective redundancy usable by a specific observer, models accessibility through a noisy-threshold aperture function, and introduces a continuity measure governing an observer’s capacity to integrate records over time. Classicality becomes a
decomposition-indexed property
, not a global feature of the universal wavefunction.
Applied to
Wigner’s Friend
and
Frauchiger–Renner
, the framework dissolves paradoxes by showing that cross-agent inferences fail precisely in regimes where effective accessibility is low. The paper outlines experimental signatures, including observer-dependent classicality thresholds and flow-disruption tests, offering a route toward
empirical constraints on observer-relative quantum structure
.
